contract.direct_answer:
For pronephric filtration onset, the fluid-dynamic readouts that matter are (1) flow velocity — the local speed/direction of fluid movement through the developing nephron lumen and pronephric duct, captured as flow vectors; (2) pressure fields — the intraluminal/transmural pressure gradients that must build for glomerular filtration to begin; and (3) shear stress — the wall/segment shear that developing tubular and podocyte-lineage cells experience, which is a candidate mechanical cue for maturation and filtration onset. The RN7 niche ("Mecánica activa y dinámica de fluidos") is the resource that explicitly carries these: it provides cell/segment/node-indexed flow vectors, velocity, and pressure as tabular files (.csv/.tsv), together with high-density 3D meshes. In the biology-context corpus, CORPUS-2026-0003 establishes the zebrafish pronephros as an in vivo model for when/how renal (nephron) development and function initiate, which is the developmental process these readouts would be applied to.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT on mesh formats: The question presupposes .vtu/.cgns mesh containers. The provided RN7 description states only that flow scalars/vectors are carried in .csv/.tsv and that "high-density 3D meshes" are provided, but the retrieved text is truncated and does NOT confirm the specific container format(s) (.vtu, .cgns, or other) that carry the mesh + fields. So I cannot verify from this bundle that .vtu or .cgns specifically are used. What I can support: velocity, pressure, and (by segment/node indexing) shear-relevant fields are in .csv/.tsv, associated with high-density 3D meshes of unspecified format.
alternatives_considered: That the meshes are stored specifically as .vtu or .cgns as the question assumes — not confirmable from the truncated RN7 description, which only names .csv/.tsv explicitly.

That shear is directly provided as a field rather than derived — the bundle lists velocity and pressure explicitly; shear is inferable from segment/node-indexed velocity gradients but is not named verbatim.

That RN6 (passive biomechanics/ECM stiffness) or RN8 (collective cell kinetics, migration velocity) could be the flow-dynamics source — rejected, as those cover tissue stiffness/tension and cell trajectories, not luminal fluid flow/shear.
